triage.diagnosis: The plan job's model endpoint went down mid-council. Every council session calls ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4000 — the local LiteLLM translator that .sdlc/bin/provider-settings.mjs starts via .sdlc/bin/model-bridge.mjs for the bridged model (provider.openai_models: muse-spark-1.3-contributor). That translator served its last request at 14:33:19, while Council 2/3 was still running, and then shut down; from that moment every model call in the job was refused. So the critic (49 turns, $2.02) ended without its structured_output, the arbiter made no model call at all (num_turns 1, cost 0, empty modelUsage) and its resume failed the same way, and nothing wrote work-order.json. The red step — 'Check that "Council 3/3 — arbitrate" returned its result' — is bookkeeping three steps downstream of the cause, not the cause. Nothing about the code, the plan or the issue is wrong: the proposer completed 125 turns at 14:30:16 and wrote a full 22-field plan/proposal.json. The trigger of the shutdown is not determinable from the log — it is a graceful stop with no traceback and no request after 14:33:19 — so this is a service outage, not a code, plan or repository defect. What survived (plan/proposal.json and plan/brief.md, kept in this run's plan-output artifact, id 11306157340) cannot be resumed: the plan job only ever downloads plan-inputs (sdlc-plan.yml:177-178) and plan-strategy.mjs's resume paths key on ledger.approved_work_order / validated_work_order, both null on state/36.json, so any re-entry of plan runs the council again — a resume would post 'resuming, not redoing' while redoing all of it. This is the outage class: the same shape (a died model run on the plan stage, error_type agent-runtime) hit #4 and #5 and the failure handler's cooldown carried both to done, while prior_signatures for #36 is empty. Park the plan stage for a cooldown — it backs off and a person hears about it if it outlasts four.
